blockers.quote: That night, on the bus, the whole city is lit up. Every head. Every number. All of them moving.
blockers.why: Check #11: the line only narrates what the picture shows in the next beat. The scene note has the city of chips passing the window, and the 2.5 s hold has the jogger brightening and the sleeping boy dimming. I have nothing to play except reading the picture back.
blockers.fix: Cut the three descriptive fragments and say only: "That night. The last bus." Then let the 2.5 s hold carry the city with no narration over it.

suggestions.quote: Here's how it works. Each chip is one person's chance at the one thing they'd choose... with nobody watching. It never tells you what that thing is.
suggestions.fix: That is too long for one breath at 1.1x. Split it into three takes: "Here's how it works." / "Each chip is one person's chance at the one thing they'd choose... with nobody watching." / "It never tells you what that thing is."

suggestions.quote: Zero point two. Against the family's money. And the biggest number is the right choice. Isn't it?
suggestions.fix: The "And" is a sum, not a cause. Play it as self-persuasion: "Zero point two. Against the family's money. So... the biggest number is the right choice. Isn't it?" This turns the planted line against you, and the "Isn't it?" is you daring yourself.

suggestions.quote: But Aarav's tiny number follows you into the hall. So you look for certainty. The teacher.
suggestions.fix: The three sentences run on one breath. Take "But Aarav's tiny number follows you into the hall." as one line, a breath, then "So you look for certainty." and a short "The teacher." as its own take. The narration notes already ask for this.

suggestions.quote: Then a little number lights up. Over every head.
suggestions.fix: The picture shows this, but the line orients the viewer in the first seconds, so keep it. Give it one verb to play, to tease, and trim to "Then a number lights up. Over every head."

The two lines before it ("You've been wearing the crowd's number. Like a verdict.") are in the same quiet register, so the thought can trail. Land it whole: "But yours moved. It went down." Then the next line finishes it.

suggestions.quote: The teacher? He's sitting the exam himself. Again. His three was never about you.
suggestions.fix: Two reveals sit back to back, the teacher and the topper. Add a short `> HOLD: 1 s` of bus hum between them so the topper's "Her eight was music" is a new beat, not another item on a list.

suggestions.quote: Or give it back... and let him choose?
suggestions.fix: Say it as a flat, quiet dare, not a quiz. The figure answers at once, so cut the held breath in the narration notes after "choose?" and go straight into the hand reaching for the gap.

suggestions.quote: Would you want to see your number? Tell us below.
suggestions.fix: Say it in one warm, low take with a real beat after "thwack", so the last image keeps its moment. "Tell us below" can be dropped if the comment tag already says it; the question alone is lighter.

keep.quote: You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
